# Tufte Data Graphics Aesthetics Skill for Muse

Edward Tufte's aesthetics of data graphics, drawn from Chapter 9 of The Visual Display of Quantitative Information: beauty as a by-product of clarity plus rich content, never a layer of decoration. The operating rules: default graphics to horizontal (~1.5:1 — the book's actual prescription, with Tufte's own skepticism of golden-ratio worship noted), thin lines with a strict weight hierarchy (data heaviest, scaffolding lightest), friendly-graphics craft (words spelled out, reading left-to-right, labels placed directly on lines instead of legends, color-blind-safe palettes, modest upper-and-lower serif type), integration of words, numbers, and drawing into the surrounding prose, and matching the format (sentence, table, graphic) to the data's size and the reader's task. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: an academic-flavored knowledge skill — no code, no tools, no data-integrity auditing (that belongs to its siblings, tufte-data-ink-ratio and tufte-chartjunk); use it to judge or refine a finished chart for a report or presentation, not to clean your data. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
